chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Asama Zayd Al-Shahham, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Do not approach the Prayer while you are intoxicated.' He said: 'The sleep (intoxication).'
ai.seo_question: What does 'intoxicated' mean in the context of missing or delaying prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a specific exegetical interpretation (*tafsir*) of the phrase 'do not approach prayer while intoxicated' (Surah An-Nisa 4:43), identifying 'intoxication' (*sukr*) as the state of sleep. This interpretation establishes the legal basis for the ruling that sleep nullifies the state of alertness required for valid prayer, linking physical drowsiness to the spiritual state of heedlessness described in the Quran. It highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) directly from the linguistic nuances of the Imams' explanations of Quranic verses.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahaam who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘(What about) the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:43] O you who believe! Do not go near the Prayer when you are Intoxicated?’ So heasws said: ‘The sleep’.
en.sarwar: 14. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from in a marfu‘ manner from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I dislike performing Salah (prayer) in their Masjid.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not dislike it; every Masjid is built on the grave of a prophet or the executor of the will of a prophet who was murdered and that site received a sprinkle of his blood and Allah loved to be spoken of therein. So you can perform obligatory Salah (prayer) therein as well as optional Salah (prayer) and what you need to perform as Qada’ (compensatory prayer).’”
